propositions: Historical mutation scores in signing.py and other shards are stale; pinned mutmut 3.7.0 discovers significantly more mutants (814 vs 491 recorded) including both equivalent survivors and genuine contract gaps, making old ceilings either blocking or unsafe.

Mutation gate must transition from whole-file enforcement to per-shard phased modes (advisory, ratchet, strict) with explicit manifest authority, deterministic promotion criteria, and bounded runtime to balance evidence quality against CI capacity.

Selector must map changed source, test, support files, and infrastructure to affected shards; preserve renames; report unmatched tests; fail on unresolved refs; emit explicit empty selection; and generate per-shard matrix jobs capped at 30 minutes each.

Each shard mode enforces different mutation outcomes: advisory publishes findings without blocking; ratchet preserves legacy survivors and blocks regressions on AST-identical functions; strict requires all mutants killed or individually fingerprinted as equivalent.

Execution must use fresh isolated base/head archives with no persisted verdict cache, pinned runtime concurrency (--max-children 1), generated archive-local config from manifest, and always-published structured evidence and artifacts.

Documentation and contract tests must codify phased promotion policy, manifest authority, false-positive handling, CI cadence, and eliminate legacy stale score tables to prevent regression to unsafe enforcement.
